pages.text: $(bold)Bountiful$() boards post jobs a town wants done: bring brass, kill pillagers, clear a ruin. Pay is emerald blocks, golden apples, saddles, real enchanted books, and standing with that board.$(br2)Trust pays better: at ten reputation, $(bold)sealed rumours$() (right-click: a map to a boss's home); at fifteen, deeper journals and totems; at thirty, a named weapon.
The capital's board works for everyone; a new town can craft its own. Decrees set what a board asks for; Archivist's Records pays in writings.

$(bold)Caravans & Convoys$(): merchant caravans travel between settlements with wagons, and you can run your own. Build a stop and routes open. This is the mid-game economy before rail.$(br2)Pirates and raiders know the roads too.

Late game, the $(bold)Trading Floor$() lets a train sell on a schedule: a depot in a real town, goods in, emeralds out, while you are elsewhere.$(br2)Depots need a Blueprint and a town with a bell and beds. There is no version that works in a hole in the ground.
